result:
Somewhere, there should be a museum of unfinished things.

Not failed things. Not abandoned things, exactly. Just the half-built birdhouse waiting in a garage, the novel with twelve excellent pages, the scarf that is still mostly a ball of yarn. Each exhibit would have a small card explaining what its maker hoped it might become.

I think people would leave feeling relieved. We tend to treat unfinished work as evidence against ourselves, when often it’s evidence that we were curious enough to begin. A sketch can teach you to see a face differently even if it never becomes a portrait. A garden plan can make you notice the light in your yard, even if you never plant a seed.

The museum gift shop would sell blank notebooks. No inspirational slogans on the covers. Just room to start something.
